slides.text: WHY DID THEY CALL THIS 'THE BLOODIEST 47 ACRES IN AMERICA'?
Jefferson City. The Missouri State Penitentiary took its first prisoner in 1836, the same month the Alamo fell.
It ran for 168 years. When it closed in 2004, it was the oldest working prison west of the Mississippi.
At its peak it held around 5,000 men.
1954: a riot tore through the prison. Inmates were killed. Buildings burned.
In 1967, Time magazine gave it the name: 'the bloodiest 47 acres in America.'
Sonny Liston learned to box here. About ten years later, he was heavyweight champion of the world.
In 1967 James Earl Ray escaped hidden in a bread box from the prison bakery. A year later, he killed Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
Today it runs tours and ghost hunts. Guides and guests report shapes in the cells and sounds nobody can explain.
